# Adjudication — ModMed (Modernizing Medicine), Senior Software Architect, Hyderabad

## TECHNICAL SCORE: 88.9 / 100

**Weights sum to exactly 1.00. Arithmetic, shown in full:**

`sum(weight x score) = 8.89` -> `8.89 x 10 = 88.9`. Losses sum to 11.10, and `100 - 11.10 = 88.90`. Both routes agree.

**This is the highest-scoring seat in the v2 workspace to date** — above Yes Madam at 88.375, AI-Native at 84.9 and o9 at 81.4 — and it is the only one of the four where the posting's hardest-weighted requirement is also his single deepest thread.

---

## THE BINDING CONSTRAINT: Java and Spring recency

At weight 0.22 and score 8, criterion 1 loses **4.40 points — 40% of everything this rubric loses.** It is the binding constraint by a factor of nearly three over the next item, and it has two components:

1. **Recency.** His last hands-on Java shipped February 2025 at Deque. The VoltusWave second stint, March 2025 to April 2026, is Go and Python. That is roughly eighteen months off Java against a JD that opens its required list with the words *"Deep expertise in Java, Spring, and Spring Boot"*. **No wording change touches this.** It is a fact about the calendar, and the honest response is to say it plainly and let eleven years of Java and six years of Spring Boot across two employers do the arguing.
2. **Spring-ecosystem breadth.** The record evidences Spring Boot, and only Spring Boot. Spring Cloud, Spring WebFlux and Spring Batch are all on the never-claim list, so the wider "Spring" surface a Java shop may probe cannot be claimed from anything we hold.

The second-largest loss is a surprise: **reactive/functional programming, at 1.60 points from a criterion weighted only 0.04.** Tied with DDD-by-name at 1.60. Both are named-competency gaps rather than capability gaps, and both are cheap to close in a reading week — but only one of them (DDD) can be partly closed on the résumé itself, because the substance is already his.

---

## THE SMALLEST HONEST LIFT

All four moves below use evidence **already in hand**. Not one adds a claim, and not one touches an open claim's wording.

1. **Merge the eight unmerged Deque bullets into the per-job resume.** `master/upgrad_resume.html` carries 6 Deque bullets; both live Hiration cards carry 14. The unmerged eight include **Jenkins -> GitHub Actions with ISO 27001 and 50% faster releases**, **PostgreSQL -> Amazon RDS**, a **Puppeteer regression framework cutting regression time over 50%**, the axe-core spider/scanning pipeline, run-over-run regression comparison, and **API versioning**. Four of those are directly this JD's asks (CI/CD commitment, quality discipline, API contracts). CLAUDE.md already names this "the biggest unfinished piece of resume work" — this seat is where it pays.
2. **Put the microservice split rule on the page.** professional-journey.md line 600 says it in his own words and it currently exists nowhere on the resume: *"a component became a microservice if it needed to scale independently or needed its own database. Each service owned its database; each database was multi-tenant."* That single sentence is DDD substance stated as an engineering rule, and it is the closest thing in the record to a bounded-context answer. Estimated **+0.5 on criterion 2**.
3. **Correct El Paso to the Java role it was.** The live card still describes it as .NET, hiding four of the eleven Java years from anyone reading the exported PDF. Correct text already exists in `master/upgrad_resume.html` §14 (Senior Java Developer, JSP and Java Enterprise Edition, Tennessee Gas Pipeline). This is a **correction, not a new claim**, and it is the cheapest Java-depth lift available on the seat whose hardest ask is Java. ⚠ His hand: bullet rewrites on pre-2016 roles do not survive the Hiration save. Estimated **+0.5 on criterion 1**.
4. **Name the Redis cache design instead of listing Redis.** Right now Redis is one item inside a skills line. The design is genuinely architect-grade and is all in the case studies: canonical keys, per-tenant namespacing, TTL 1h (KQ1) and TTL 6h (KQ4), **single-flight owner-token locks against cache stampede**, lock TTL derived from circuit-breaker and search timeouts with jitter, and namespace-wide invalidation on model swap. One re-vectored bullet converts the weakest criterion's cache half from a product-name gap into a design answer. Estimated **+1.0 on criterion 8**.

**Resulting ceiling: 91.2.** Arithmetic: criterion 1 to 8.5 (`0.22 x 8.5 = 1.87`, +0.11), criterion 2 to 9.5 (`0.16 x 9.5 = 1.52`, +0.08), criterion 8 to 7 (`0.04 x 7 = 0.28`, +0.04). New `sum(weight x score) = 9.12` -> **91.2**.

---

## THE HONEST CEILING: ~91.2. **95 IS NOT REACHABLE ON THIS SEAT WITHOUT FABRICATING.**

Say it plainly rather than engineering a number. The remaining ~8.8 points sit behind six things, and **every one of them is a RAMP ITEM — there is no CAPABILITY CAP anywhere on this rubric**:

| What is missing | Why it cannot be closed by writing | Label |

| Java shipped in the last 18 months | The calendar. Only time, or him confirming Java work in the VoltusWave stint that is not in the record | RAMP ITEM |
| Spring beyond Spring Boot (Cloud, WebFlux, Batch) | All three on the never-claim list | RAMP ITEM |
| DDD by name — bounded contexts, aggregates, ubiquitous language, context maps | **Zero hits across professional-journey.md and all 22 case-study files.** Substance yes, vocabulary no | RAMP ITEM |
| Reactive programming — Project Reactor, RxJava, Mono/Flux, backpressure | Zero hits. WebFlux is never-claim. Async/event-driven is adjacent, not equivalent | RAMP ITEM |
| Kafka or NATS by name | Never-claim. **Satisfied conceptually by Amazon Kinesis** per the "e.g." rule — shards map to partitions, Enhanced Fan-Out to dedicated consumer throughput | RAMP ITEM |
| A named cache grid (Hazelcast, Ignite, Coherence); HL7/FHIR for an EHR | Never-claim / absent. Neither is named in the posting | RAMP ITEM |

**The distinction matters and should be said out loud when this score is reported:** 88.9 is not the score of a candidate missing a core required technology. Every core requirement in the posting's own list is met — Java, Spring Boot, microservices, distributed systems, relational and NoSQL databases, event streaming (via Kinesis, per the "e.g." rule), Docker, Kubernetes, low-latency, observability, CI/CD. The 11.1 points come from recency on the heaviest criterion and from named-competency vocabulary on two lighter ones. A 95 here would require writing Kafka, WebFlux or DDD terminology into his record, and that is precisely the trade CLAUDE.md forbids: an honest 88.9 beats an invented 95, because the invented one gets found in the room.

## HONESTY FLAGS FROM `jd.md` — HONOURED, NOT RESOLVED

- **"Event Streaming (e.g. Kafka, NATS)"** — read generously as the scoring rule requires. Scored **MET** at 9/10 on his two-stream Amazon Kinesis Enhanced Fan-Out design, confirmed in production. **The words Kafka and NATS appear nowhere in this rubric as his**, and must not appear in any workspace artefact as his.

His call alone, per CLAUDE.md. Four sit inside this rubric's evidence and none has been resolved, softened or rewritten here:

This seat's Deque *Stewarded* bullet folds them, on master/merge_proposal.html's reasoning that Aurora IS RDS. Both halves are his own card's and both have gone out, so nothing is scrubbed — but the backups **3–4 hours daily** and **deploy errors 40%** were recorded against the migration, not against the version upgrade. **The one line worth settling before the export runs.**

⛔ **No interview prep built.** Reaffirmed 2026-08-26 — prep waits until a company responds. Flagging these for later prep is the whole of what happens here.

## NON-TECHNICAL / FUNCTIONAL SCORE: NOT COMPUTED

**v2 computes no non-technical score, and none is invented here.** Industry domain, commercial context and representation are informational only, never a gate, and never a drag on the technical number. Criterion 9 above scores HIPAA-grade *engineering* — PHI handling, audit trails, access governance, certification-driven availability — which is technical work; it is deliberately not "healthcare industry familiarity", and the criterion text says so.

None of these touched the 88.9.

- **Location — clean, and unusually so.** Hyderabad, which is where he lives (set 2026-08-25). No relocation question exists on this seat at all. Relocation is never a scoring constraint in any case.
